solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Agitated celebrity starts to take liberties each day (8)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of words are their first letters, and 'starts to' takes them from each of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of take, liberties, each
D is the standard abbreviation for day

annotation.surface: A famous person grows restless and starts taking liberties every day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' reaches over three words, not one, so it gives three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone startled is jolted and agitated by a sudden shock.

entries.clue: Is turning up holding party food (6)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters bottom to top
indicatorNotes.holding: the reversed IS holds the party inside it

blocks.note: a camp is a party or faction

annotation.surface: Someone arrives at a party with food.
annotation.walkthrough: Party here is a faction, as in the rival camps of a political dispute, not a celebration.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: scampi, fried breaded langoustine tails, is a dish.

entries.clue: Conflict from clique with no leader (6)

indicatorNotes.with no leader: the leader of a word is its first letter, so a word with no leader has lost it

annotation.surface: Fighting breaks out in a group that has lost its head.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'no leader' a political story; it is only the first letter of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: soldiers in action are engaged in armed conflict.

entries.clue: Section of totem pole in grave, say (5)

indicatorNotes.Section of: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

annotation.surface: Part of a totem pole stands in a grave.
annotation.walkthrough: Grave looks like a burial place; in music it is a very slow tempo marking, and 'say' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: grave is one of the musical speed markings, like largo or adagio.

entries.clue: Old nurse’s offers (7)

annotation.surface: A retired nurse's offers.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', making nurse a verb: she tends.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to extend a hand or an invitation is to hold it out, to offer it.

entries.clue: Sounds from clarinets, essentially – piercing things you blow? (6)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of something is its core, so the very middle letter of the word
indicatorNotes.piercing: the letter pierces into the other word

blocks.note: the middle letter of the nine in CLARINETS

annotation.surface: Clarinettists produce noises, and the question is what you blow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Things you blow' reads like wind instruments after 'clarinets', but here it means noses.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both plural nouns for things heard.

entries.clue: Aida perhaps changed into outfit (9)

indicatorNotes.changed: letters that are changed are put in a different order

annotation.surface: A woman called Aida changes into an outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word but is the anagram fodder, and outfit means an organisation, not clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: an outfit is a business or organisation, as is a company's whole operation.

entries.clue: Astonish sir with super bust (8)

indicatorNotes.bust: something bust is broken, and broken letters are reassembled in a new order

annotation.surface: A superb bust of a knight stuns everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: Bust reads as a sculpture; it means broken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to take someone aback with the unexpected.

entries.clue: Dread hearing possibly about US power (8)

indicatorNotes.about: the sense goes round the rest

annotation.surface: Fear of listening in on American power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks hearing as one example of a sense, not a request to hear something.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: suspense is the anxious dread of waiting to learn what happens.

entries.clue: Goes tense wrapped in horrible pet’s mat (8)

indicatorNotes.wrapped in: the T goes inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.horrible: something horrible is a mess, and a mess of letters is a new order

annotation.surface: A pet's awful mat makes someone tense up.
annotation.walkthrough: Goes is a noun here, not the verb the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural noun sense: having a few goes at something means making tries at it.

entries.clue: Carrot’s regularly hidden in the man’s suit (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
indicatorNotes.hidden in: the letters are placed inside HE'S

blocks.note: the even letters of CARROT: cArRoT

annotation.surface: A carrot is secretly tucked into a man's suit.
annotation.walkthrough: Suit is the card suit, not clothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

entries.clue: What turns up on a parking lot (4)

indicatorNotes.turns up: in a down clue, read upwards

annotation.surface: Something turns up in a car park.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parking lot' reads as one American phrase; lot is split off as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal quantity sense: a heap of work, like a lot of work, is a large amount.

entries.clue: In favour of new unit of weight, say (9)

blocks.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

annotation.surface: Someone backs a new measure of weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma hides that 'say' is the definition, not a hint that the weight is an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to utter a word aloud, or to declare formally.

entries.clue: Admit a reduced urge (5)

indicatorNotes.reduced: a reduced word is made smaller, here by losing its last letter

blocks.note: GREED, an urge to have more, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone confesses to a diminished craving.
annotation.walkthrough: Admit is a concession, as in 'I admit you have a point'.
annotation.definitionFit: A concession sense: to grant that a point is true, as in 'I admit that'.

entries.clue: Requests unopened face coverings (4)

indicatorNotes.unopened: a word that is unopened has not got its opening, its first letter

annotation.surface: Orders for masks that nobody unpacks.
annotation.walkthrough: Unopened suggests unwrapped parcels; it only strips the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs in the same third-person form.

entries.clue: Happy if a diet’s altered after start of September (9)

indicatorNotes.after: the rearranged letters come after S
indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone is content once their diet has been changed in September.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is part of the fodder, supplying the last S of the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: content, pleased that a need has been met.

entries.clue: Ministers – annoying people embracing religious instruction (7)

indicatorNotes.embracing: the outer word holds the inner

blocks.note: RI = religious instruction, a school subject

annotation.surface: Irritating clergy pushing religion on people.
annotation.walkthrough: Ministers looks political; here it means clergy.
annotation.definitionFit: A religious sense: ministers of the church, as opposed to ministers of state.

entries.clue: Disgraceful things about wearing shoes (8)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the C is inside the shoes, as feet are

annotation.surface: Shameful footwear choices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About wearing shoes' reads like fashion chatter; about is only a C inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: events that cause public outrage and disgrace.

entries.clue: Married a smarter femme fatale (3-5)

annotation.surface: A well-dressed seductress has got married.
annotation.walkthrough: Smarter means better turned out, not cleverer.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a seductive woman who uses men and discards them.

entries.clue: Something that might be under glass vessel (7)

annotation.definition: Something that might be under glass

blocks.clueFragment: Something that might be under glass
blocks.note: a mat set under a drinking glass
a ship that trades along the coast

annotation.surface: Something kept under a glass vessel, like a museum display.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glass vessel' reads as one phrase; the split falls between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a small mat protecting a table from a glass, and a ship that sails from port to port along a coast.

entries.clue: Regret concealing a second stratagem (4)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the outer word hides the S

annotation.surface: Someone regrets hiding a backup plan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A second' is one letter S, with the 'a' meaning one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cunning trick meant to deceive.

entries.clue: Long backbone but no head (4)

indicatorNotes.but no head: the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

annotation.surface: A long spine with no skull on top.
annotation.walkthrough: Long is a verb here, to yearn, not the adjective the surface uses.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to yearn for something absent.

entries.clue: Mate’s quiet with a little resistance before opening up (7)

indicatorNotes.before: these letters come before the next
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, read upwards

blocks.note: a rent (a tear) is an opening, read upwards

annotation.surface: A friend goes quiet, offering little resistance before opening up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening up' reads as confiding; it is a rent turned upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a spouse or companion, or a colleague in British 'mate' usage.

entries.clue: Chucked king’s chair over the phone (6)

indicatorNotes.over the phone: on the phone you only hear a word, so it is its sound that counts

blocks.note: the throne is a king's chair

annotation.surface: Someone describes chucking out the king's chair during a phone call.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the wordplay is the sound of the royal seat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the past participle of throw, matching chucked.

entries.clue: Match official enters for a favour (6)

indicatorNotes.enters: the official enters the other word, going inside it

annotation.surface: A referee walks in asking a favour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For a' looks like a link; it is PER, as in 'ten pounds per head'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to like one option better than another.

entries.clue: Wants massages by the sound of it (5)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: the word is judged by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

annotation.surface: Someone wants a massage.
annotation.walkthrough: The silent K of the massage word drops out when spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: requires, lacks, as in 'the house wants painting'.

entries.clue: Sweep emergency room – patient may need this (9)

blocks.note: a sweep of land is a stretch

annotation.surface: A hospital emergency room, where a patient needs something.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash separates the wordplay from a definition that describes rather than names.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a patient who cannot walk is carried on this.

entries.clue: Bit upset with small gins? (5)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, set upside down

blocks.note: a part is a bit, read upwards

annotation.surface: Someone is a bit put out by small measures of gin.
annotation.walkthrough: A gin is also an old word for a snare, which is how the question mark hints away from drinks.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense: a gin, from engine, is a snare for catching game.

entries.clue: Realise bikini attaches partly from the back (6)

indicatorNotes.partly: only part of the words is used
indicatorNotes.from the back: reading from the back starts at the end and runs to the front

annotation.surface: Someone notices the bikini fastens at the back.
annotation.walkthrough: Realise means achieve, as in realising an ambition, not notice.
annotation.definitionFit: An achievement sense: to realise a goal is to reach it.

entries.clue: This could make snake slither away (5,3)

annotation.definition: This could make snake slither away

blocks.note: read the answer as an instruction: a word followed by an anagram indicator, whose letters rearrange into SNAKE
the plain meaning: to leave quietly

annotation.surface: Something that makes a snake slide off.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, SNEAK OFF means 'SNEAK, jumbled', which makes SNAKE: the answer is itself a clue for the word in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to leave furtively, which is how a snake slithers away.

entries.clue: Tramp’s short trousers (6)

indicatorNotes.short: a word cut short loses its end

blocks.note: British and Australian slang for trousers

annotation.surface: A vagrant's short trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: Tramp is a verb, to walk heavily, not the vagrant of the surface; STRIDES is slang for trousers.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to walk with long heavy steps.

entries.clue: Someone completing sentence in prose modified by editor, finally (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally points to the end of the word, its last letter

annotation.surface: An editor finishes revising a sentence in someone's prose.
annotation.walkthrough: Sentence is a prison term, not a line of prose.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: someone serving a jail term until it is complete.
